record.paper_title: Recent Results and Open Problems in Evolutionary Multiobjective Optimization
record.original_question: How can multi-objective evolutionary algorithms scale in the decision-variable space, especially for problems with hundreds or thousands of decision variables, rather than only scaling in the number of objectives?

evidence.quote: What about scalability in decision variable space?
There is almost no work on this topic

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a multi-objective optimization problem of the form

  minimize  F(x) = (f_1(x), f_2(x), ..., f_m(x)),    x ∈ X ⊆ R^n,

where m ≥ 2 is the number of objectives and n is the number of decision variables. A multi-objective evolutionary algorithm (MOEA) is a population-based stochastic search procedure that maintains a set of candidate solutions in X and iteratively applies variation operators (e.g., recombination and mutation) and selection mechanisms based on Pareto dominance, decomposition, or quality indicators in order to approximate the Pareto-optimal set { x ∈ X : there is no y ∈ X with F(y) ≤ F(x) and F(y) ≠ F(x) }.

Most classical MOEAs (such as NSGA-II, MOEA/D, SPEA2, IBEA) were designed and evaluated for problems with a modest number of decision variables (typically n ≤ 30), and their empirical performance is known to deteriorate sharply as n grows large.

Problem. Develop multi-objective evolutionary algorithms whose performance (in terms of convergence to and coverage of the Pareto front, and computational cost) scales gracefully as the number of decision variables n grows into the hundreds or thousands, rather than only scaling with the number of objectives m. In particular, design representations, variation operators, decision-variable analysis/grouping strategies, dimensionality-reduction techniques, or co-evolutionary frameworks, and provide theoretical or empirical guarantees that the resulting algorithms remain effective on large-scale multi-objective optimization problems (LSMOPs) with n in the range of 10^2–10^4.
artifact.status_search_result: Since the question was posed, a substantial body of work on large-scale multi-objective evolutionary optimization (LSMOEA) has appeared. Surveys (e.g., "Evolutionary Large-Scale Multi-Objective Optimization: A Survey", ACM Computing Surveys 2021; "Evolutionary Computation for Large-scale Multi-objective Optimization: A Decade of Progresses", 2021) classify existing approaches into divide-and-conquer/cooperative co-evolution, dimensionality-reduction, and enhanced-search methods, and document concrete algorithms scaling to thousands of variables. The general design question is thus actively researched and partially addressed by practical algorithms, but no definitive theoretically optimal framework exists, so the broader research challenge remains open.

status_evidence.title: Evolutionary Large-Scale Multi-Objective Optimization: A Survey
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys algorithms tackling MOPs with large numbers of decision variables, categorizing divide-and-conquer, dimensionality reduction, and enhanced search approaches.
status_evidence.claim: A growing literature directly addresses MOEA scalability in decision-variable space, indicating partial progress on the question.

status_evidence.title: Evolutionary Computation for Large-scale Multi-objective Optimization: A Decade of Progresses
status_evidence.snippet: Reviews a decade of progress on LSMOPs with hundreds to thousands of decision variables.
status_evidence.claim: Substantial methodological progress has been made, but the area is still active and unresolved overall.

status_evidence.title: Research on MOEAs Based on Large-Scale Decision Variable Analysis
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2024) work continues to propose decision-variable analysis and grouping techniques for LSMOPs.
status_evidence.claim: Ongoing recent research confirms the question is partially solved and still active.
